**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Economics 2 (0725), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2025. Duration: three hours.**

Instructions to candidates: Answer FIVE questions, choosing AT LEAST TWO from each section. All questions carry equal marks.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.
incertitudes: Règle de choix : le sujet impose « Answer FIVE questions, choosing AT LEAST TWO from each section » (5 questions en tout, au moins 2 par section). `regles_choix` ne sait exprimer que « n parmi m » : chaque section porte la règle minimale (2 sur 4) ; la règle « 5 en tout » n'est pas exprimable et figure dans `introduction_markdown`.

Points : le sujet n'imprime que les points de chaque partie (a) et (b), jamais le total de la question ; `points` de l'exercice est donc laissé vide. Les parties de chaque question totalisent 20 (10+10, 12+8, 12+8, 8+12, 10+10, 5+15, 8+12, 8+12), conformément à « All questions carry equal marks ». Q5(a) imprime « (5+5 marks) » pour (i) et (ii) et Q6(b) « (5+5+5 marks) » pour (i), (ii), (iii) : ces points sont regroupés dans la sous-question (10 et 15). Aucun écart constaté entre les points imprimés.

Sujet scanné (filigrane gcerevision.com en travers des pages, sans conséquence sur la lisibilité) ; aucun corrigé officiel : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées, les chiffres des exemples (FCFA, quantités, taux) sont hypothétiques et recalculés avec Python ; aucune statistique réelle n'est avancée. Les repères institutionnels cités (BEAC, franc CFA arrimé à l'euro) relèvent de la culture générale, pas du sujet.

Défauts d'impression du sujet, conservés tels quels : Q2(a) « With the aid of a diagram (s) ... minimum and maximum price legislations » (pluriel et « (s) » fautifs), Q4(b) « demand for higher wages », Q6(b) « How effective can interest rate be used to achieve » (formulation incorrecte). Les questions de la Section B sont numérotées 5 à 8 (pas de renumérotation « B1 »). Le sujet tient en deux pages (page de garde et questions) : aucune question n'est coupée ni illisible.

Figure fig-1 (Q2(a)) : schéma produit pour le corrigé (matplotlib, unités arbitraires, aucun chiffre réel) ; ce n'est pas une figure du sujet. Les autres diagrammes (monopole contre concurrence monopolistique, droit de douane) sont décrits dans les corrigés, sans PNG.

questions.enonce_markdown:
What do you understand by expansionary monetary policy?

(5 marks)

How effective can interest rate be used to achieve:

(i) full employment?

(ii) economic growth ?

(iii) price stability?

(5+5+5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** The rate of interest is the main tool of monetary policy: it is the **cost of borrowing** and the **reward for saving**. Its effectiveness differs according to the objective and to the structure of the economy.

**(i) Full employment (5 marks).**
- *How it works:* a **fall in the interest rate** makes loans cheaper, so firms invest more and households borrow and spend more. Aggregate demand rises, firms increase output and hire more workers: **demand-deficient (cyclical) unemployment** falls.
- *Effectiveness is limited when:* **investment is interest-inelastic** (firms are pessimistic and will not borrow even at low rates, a "liquidity trap"); there is **structural, frictional or seasonal unemployment**, which more demand cannot cure and which needs training, mobility and improved information; banks do not pass the lower rate on to borrowers or are reluctant to lend to risky small firms; there are **time lags** of months before the effect on jobs; much of the economy is **informal** and outside the banking system, so interest rates reach few workers; and a large part of employment depends on agriculture and public spending.
- *Judgement:* effective against cyclical unemployment in a developed banking system, but only **partly effective** against the unemployment of a developing economy like Cameroon's.

**(ii) Economic growth (5 marks).**
- *How it works:* low interest rates raise **investment** in capital goods and infrastructure, which expands productive capacity and the long-run growth rate; they also increase demand, which raises output in the short run. Where a **higher rate** attracts savings into banks, more funds are available for loans (a supply of loanable funds).
- *Effectiveness is limited when:* growth is held back by **supply-side constraints** (poor roads, electricity and water, weak institutions, low skills, lack of technology), which the interest rate cannot solve; the **volume of savings and bank credit is low**; high rates needed for other reasons (stability of the currency) discourage investment; **expectations and political stability** matter more than the cost of credit; and low rates may encourage consumption or imports instead of investment.
- *Judgement:* the interest rate can **support** growth in the short and medium term, but sustained growth depends mainly on **supply-side policies** and investment in human and physical capital.

**(iii) Price stability (5 marks).**
- *How it works:* a **rise in the interest rate** makes borrowing dearer and saving more attractive, so consumption and investment fall, aggregate demand falls and **demand-pull inflation** is controlled. It can also strengthen the exchange rate and so lower the price of imports.
- *Effectiveness is limited when:* inflation is **cost-push or imported** (higher prices of oil, food or imported inputs, or a poor harvest), which a higher interest rate does not cure and may worsen by raising firms' costs and lowering output; **time lags** are long and uncertain; many people **do not use banks**, so the transmission is weak; and in the CEMAC zone the **common central bank sets the rates** for all member countries and the CFA franc is **pegged to the euro**, so Cameroon alone cannot choose an interest rate suited to its own situation.
- *Judgement:* **effective against demand-pull inflation**, much less against cost-push or imported inflation.

**Conclusion.** The interest rate is an easy and flexible instrument but its effect is **uncertain and limited** in a developing economy: it works best for price stability against excess demand, less well for full employment and growth, which require supply-side measures and fiscal policy as well.
